# `contracts/` — the language-neutral fixtures

Centraid is three languages — Rust, Kotlin/Swift and TypeScript ([#1020](https://github.com/srikanth235/centraid/issues/1020)). A fixture that lives inside one of them is a fixture the others cannot be held to, so every fact more than one of them must agree about lives here, as data, in a form each language's tests can read without a bridge.

**The rule.** Every fixture under `contracts/` is read by a test, and a fixture with a generator is regenerated by that generator, never edited by hand. Two kinds live here:

- **Generated fixtures** — reproduced from a live source (a Rust binary, `packages/design`, a proto) on every run or by a named command, with `git diff --exit-code` as the drift check.
- **Frozen goldens** — the golden corpora, the registries transcription, the app parity fixtures under `apps/` and the applier oracle were produced once from the TypeScript tree removed in [#1020](https://github.com/srikanth235/centraid/issues/1020). Their generators went with it. They are now fixed expectations that the Rust tests compare against; a change to one is a deliberate edit reviewed as a change in behaviour, not a regeneration.

## The tree

| Path | What it is | Kept current by |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `golden/issue-1020/` | **The baseline corpus**: a vault frozen at the ladder head (`user_version` 11), `vault.db.gz` and its `manifest.json`. The shape `crates/vault` founds a file from (#1020, **D-1020-D1-1**). | The database is frozen. Its manifest (the row digests `crates/ontology/tests/golden_vault.rs` compares against) is regenerated from the corpus: `cargo run -p centraid-ontology --bin export-golden-manifest -- contracts/golden/issue-1020 > contracts/golden/issue-1020/manifest.json`. |
| `golden/issue-929/` | The #929 **checkpoint** corpus, frozen at `user_version` 7 — the low end of the accepted window. | The database is frozen and never re-cut; its manifest is regenerated the same way. |
| `golden/issue-1020/vault-ddl.sql` | The **baseline corpus's** `sqlite_master` — every schema object that carries DDL, ordered by type then name. A description of the frozen v0 file, beside the file it describes. | `cargo run -p centraid-ontology --bin export-ddl -- contracts/golden/issue-1020/vault.db.gz > contracts/golden/issue-1020/vault-ddl.sql`; `crates/ontology/tests/fixtures.rs` re-renders it and diffs on every run. |
| `schema/vault-ddl.sql` | The **shape a new vault founds**: the `sqlite_master` of a file founded at the ladder head, ordered by type then name. The language-neutral statement of the shape a vault file has, and the one every app's fixture vault is built from. It is the corpus's shape plus whatever the rungs above the baseline do (#1029). | `cargo run -p centraid-vault --bin export-ladder-ddl > contracts/schema/vault-ddl.sql`; `crates/vault/tests/ladder_ddl.rs` founds a vault and diffs on every run. |
| `schema/v0-registries.json` | The model's registries as JSON: ontology version, both ends of the `user_version` window, the ontology packs and machinery bands, the audit band, private tables, local tables, sealed columns, the entity catalog with lifecycle and deletion roles, content references, retention windows and the snapshot exclusions. The file name records where it was transcribed from. | Frozen golden; `crates/ontology/src/registries.rs` embeds it with `include_str!`. |
| `apps/<app>/` | Each app's parity fixtures — typically `rows.json` (every row the app's queries read), `queries.json` (`{query, input, output}` at fixed inputs), `commands.json` (a replayable command script, refusals included) and `scenarios.json` (the ontology scenarios that touch the app). Rows rather than a `vault.db.gz`, because the bootstrap mints UUIDv7 ids and a database file is therefore not byte-reproducible, and because a compressed database is not a diff anyone reads; Rust reconstructs the file from these rows and `schema/vault-ddl.sql`. Every identifier is canonicalised to first-appearance order and every host-clock instant to `<host-clock>`. `apps/docs/`, `apps/people/` and `apps/photos/` carry their own README. | Frozen goldens, read by `crates/apps/<app>/tests/parity.rs`. |
| `migrations/` | The forward-only ladder's rungs, each BOTH the migration `crates/vault` embeds and the fixture under `contracts/` (D-1020-D1-13). **One rung today**: `001_baseline.sql` is what a new vault founds — the whole schema and the rows founding seeds (the money categories scheme and its concepts) — **squashed on 2026-10-15** from the fifteen rungs that came before it, because nothing had shipped ([Q-1029-1](../docs/decisions.md), [#1029](https://github.com/srikanth235/centraid/issues/1029)); the same squash renamed `agent_command` and `agent_command_invocation` to `command_definition` and `command_invocation` (Q-1029-3), and on 2026-10-16, still before any release, the baseline was amended once more: the other four `agent_*` tables became `command_capability`, `command_invocation_check`, `command_evidence` and `command_explanation`, `access_device` and `access_device_secret` (and the two columns naming them) went, and Tally's CHECK value left `schedule_recurrence_exception`. `999_fails.sql` is not a rung at all: it is a migration that fails mid-way on purpose, `crates/vault/src/migrations.rs`'s fixture for a rung that rolls back whole. **The ladder is appended to, never edited — including its comments**: a file in the field has already run the old text, so an edit changes what a fresh file gets and nothing else. The next schema change is a `002_<name>.sql` registered in `LADDER`. | The baseline is cut by `cargo run -p centraid-vault --bin export-baseline > contracts/migrations/001_baseline.sql`, which founds a vault from the embedded ladder and renders it (byte for byte while the ladder is one rung; the squash of the whole ladder once a rung is appended); `crates/vault/tests/baseline.rs` and `migrations::tests` prove it. A rung is written by hand and proven by a test under `crates/vault/tests/`; the head's DDL is regenerated by `cargo run -p centraid-vault --bin export-ladder-ddl > contracts/schema/vault-ddl.sql` and checked by `ladder_ddl.rs`. |
| `crypto/` | The crypto vectors, each with the test that reads it beside it: `identity-vectors.json` (the account key, three vaults' identity/box/root leaves and the rendered safety number, from BIP39's zero-entropy phrase — the one fixture this repository generates), `rfc9180-vectors.json` (RFC 9180 Appendix A.1, transcribed from the CFRG file; **nothing here produced these bytes**), `blake3-vectors.json` (the keyed hash and the KDF as primitives) and `sealed-vectors.json` (`centraid-sealed/2`: its keys, names and sealed samples, opened on every run, [#1080](https://github.com/srikanth235/centraid/issues/1080)). | `CENTRAID_UPDATE_FIXTURES=1 cargo test -p <crate>` regenerates and the comparison still runs, so the variable is a generator and never a way to go green. **Freely regenerated until the first release** ([D-1020-R1, dropped](../docs/decisions.md#supersessions-closed-by-1029)); after it they become format commitments and the tests' own headers say what must be deleted to make that true. |
| `time/` | The civil-time and recurrence cases — DST transitions and occurrence expansion — read by `crates/vault`'s one time engine. | Hand-authored; see [`time/README.md`](time/README.md). |
| `screens/` | Protobuf screen-state fixtures, a `.textproto` and its `.bin` per state, decoded by both the Kotlin and the Swift side. | `bun contracts/tools/build-screen-fixtures.ts`, then `bun run format`; `git diff --exit-code contracts/screens`. |
| `assist/export/` | The **native tool task's export**: the tool schemas, the kind card, the date-expression schema, the phrase and error tables, the metadata table, the rendered system prompts and `identity.json` (the model's tokenizer id and chat markers), as `nativetools export` writes them. Read by the Python trainer and scorer (`experiments/toolchat/native`) and the data generators; see [`assist/export/README.md`](assist/export/README.md). | `cargo run -p centraid-nativetools --bin nativetools -- export contracts/assist/export`; `crates/nativetools/tests/export_fixture.rs` re-renders it and diffs on every run. |
| `ledgers/` | The gate's down-only budgets — see [`crates/xtask/README.md`](../crates/xtask/README.md). | The ratchet in `crates/xtask`; a number only falls. |
| `handoff/` | **Historical hand-off notes**, not current state: patches and READMEs an earlier wave left for a later one, several of them for planes since deleted (assist, automations, the extension, the desktop e2e lane). Kept as evidence; nothing reads them. | Append-only by convention; a note is never rewritten. |
| `tools/` | The generators that are not Rust binaries. The design emitters (`export-native-theme.ts`, which calls `export-native-catalog.ts` and `export-design-corpus.ts`) lower `packages/design` into the committed native theme and identity corpus. | — |

## The version window is two numbers, and both are embedded

`schema/v0-registries.json` carries **both ends** of the `PRAGMA user_version` window the vault accepts (#1020, **D-1020-A1**):

- `userVersion` — what the #929 **checkpoint** corpus was frozen at.
- `ladderUserVersion` — the ladder head, what the baseline corpus was frozen at.

They are both here, rather than one here and one in a manifest, because `crates/ontology` embeds this file and nothing else: `Vault::open` has to know the window without reading a repository path at runtime. A file above the ladder head is refused as a downgrade, one below the corpus as needing a forward migration this crate does not have. `crates/ontology/tests/fixtures.rs` asserts each number against the manifest of the corpus at that end, so the embedded window and the committed corpora cannot disagree.
